surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Marchenko scores in his return to Columbus
paras: Jake Christiansen struck first for the Blue Jackets early in the first. Kirill Marchenko made it 1-1 for Toronto on the power play midway through the period, in his first game back in Columbus. The Maple Leafs’ Jake McCabe left in the first period and didn’t return. The next day, he was listed as day to day with a face injury. The second period belonged to the Maple Leafs. William Nylander gave the Maple Leafs the lead early in the period, and Auston Matthews made it 3-1, 46 seconds later, in his 700th NHL game. Easton Cowan stretched the lead to 4-1 shorthanded less than four minutes later. Jack Roslovic made it 5-1 midway through the second. Columbus pulled Jet Greaves after five goals and turned to Cam Talbot for the rest of the second. The Maple Leafs went just over 18 minutes without a shot on goal, from midway through the second to midway through the third, while the Blue Jackets put 18 on net. Zack MacEwen and Erik Gudbranson dropped the gloves late in the second. Charlie Coyle cut Toronto’s lead to 5-2 early in the third. Marshall Rifai, undrafted and in his fifth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Morgan Rielly, with just over three minutes left to make it 6-2 for the Leafs. Three players had three-point nights: Roslovic with a goal and two assists, Cowan with a goal and two assists, and Rielly with three assists.

The Blue Jackets outshot the Maple Leafs 37-22, but the Maple Leafs’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Anthony Stolarz, who gave up five goals in Utah in his last start, made 35 saves for the Maple Leafs.
The Maple Leafs killed all six Blue Jackets power plays. The Maple Leafs moved to 5-4-2 and climbed to fifth in the Atlantic, while the Blue Jackets dropped to 3-5-0, still last in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Auston Matthews scored again against Columbus, and has eight goals in nine games against them since 2023-24.
Charlie Coyle scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 11.
Nick Blankenburg was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Marshall Rifai played instead.
Three of the preview’s four calls held.
